{{Short description|Unofficial holiday}}
'''Square Root Day''' is an [[Holiday#Unofficial holidays|unofficial holiday]] celebrated on days when both the day of the month and the month are the [[square root]] of the last two [[numerical digit|digits]] of the year.<ref>{{cite news |title= A day getting to the root |last= Wong |first= Nicole C. |work= The Mercury News |url= http://www.mercurynews.com/mld/mercurynews/news/7854616.htm  |date= 2004-02-02 |accessdate= 2007-02-20 |archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20040818204722/http://www.mercurynews.com/mld/mercurynews/news/7854616.htm |archivedate = 2004-08-18}}</ref> For example, the last Square Root Day was Monday, May 5, 2025 (5/5/25), and the next Square Root Day will be Friday, June 6, 2036 (6/6/36).{{Update after|2036|6|6}} The final Square Root Day of the 21st century will occur on Tuesday, September 9, 2081. Square Root Days fall upon the same nine dates each century. Notably, May 5, 2025, which also coincided with [[Cinco de Mayo]], is a perfect Square Root Day, because 5 multiplied by 5 equals 25, and 45 multiplied by 45 equals 2025.<ref>{{cite news |title=Math lovers delight - today is square root day |work=NPR |url=https://www.npr.org/2025/05/05/nx-s1-5387370/square-root-day-today |accessdate=2025-05-05}}</ref> 

Ron Gordon, a [[Redwood City, California]], high school teacher, created the first Square Root Day for Wednesday, September 9, 1981 (9/9/81).  Gordon remains the holiday's [[publicist]], sending [[news release]]s to world [[News media|media]] outlets.<ref>{{cite news |title=Have a rootin' tootin' Square Root Day |last=Hill |first=Angela |work=Oakland Tribune |url= http://www.insidebayarea.com/oaklandtribune/localnews/ci_11821782?source=rss |date=2009-03-02 |accessdate= 2009-03-02}}</ref> Gordon's daughter set up a [[Facebook]] group where people can share how they were celebrating the day.<ref>{{cite news|title=Math Fans to Celebrate Square Root Day |work=Yahoo News |url=https://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20090303/ap_on_fe_st/odd_square_root_day |date=2009-03-02 |access-date=2009-03-02 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090306184913/http://news.yahoo.com/s/ap/20090303/ap_on_fe_st/odd_square_root_day |archive-date=March 6, 2009 }}</ref>

One suggested way of celebrating the holiday is by eating [[radish]]es or other [[root vegetable]]s cut into shapes with square [[Cross section (geometry)|cross sections]] (thus creating a "square root").<ref>{{cite news |title=Square Root Day revelers to party like it's 3/3/09 |last=Musil |first=Steven |work=cnet news |url=  http://news.cnet.com/8301-11386_3-10186121-76.html?part=rss&subj=news&tag=2547-1_3-0-5 |date=2009-03-02 |accessdate=2009-03-02}}</ref>

== Full list ==
Square Root Day occurs on the following dates each century:

*1/1/01
*2/2/04
*3/3/09
*4/4/16
*5/5/25
*6/6/36
*7/7/49
*8/8/64
*9/9/81
<!-- PLEASE do not add 10/10/00 (or 2100). 10 is not the square root of 00; please re-read the definition of Square Root Day in the text. Further, in centuries after the current one, no case can be made that 10/10/2200, 10/10/2300, etc. is a Square Root Day even by extension. Thank you. [[User:Finell]] -->
